title.narrative: ToGETHER - Promoting locally led transformative humanitarian action in eight countries

description.narrative: 5 Local Humanitarian Partners(LHPs) are the primary participants of the program. In addition, each LHP will be mentoring 3 local peer organizations, adding up to a total of 15 humanitarian peer organizations in Pakistan. Humanitarian Operation andInnovationFacility-funded emergency interventions will address individuals affected or vulnerable to crises and disasters between 2024 to 2027 in the respetive program countries. Based on vulnerability criteria, refugees, internally displaced people, disaster-affected populations and vulnerable groups, particularly women will be offered assistance.

Project outcome:5 local humanitarian partners (LHPs) contribute to humanitarian action through authentic leadership, institutional capacity, advocacy, and operations in accordance with international humanitarian standards.The development of ToGETHER 2.0 is the result of sustained progress built on the collective experiences gained through ToGETHER 1.0, on the Grand Bargain (GB) and localization efforts with an emphasis on contributing to Grand Bargain 3.0. This phase accentuates the promotion of local leadership, humanitarian-centered approaches, mentoring local humanitarian peer NGOs capacity strengthening, anticipatory humanitarian action, piloting risk-sharing, and advocating for efficient, effective, and fair humanitarian architecture.

The project builds on achievements of the first phase of the ToGETHER program (PAK 1109) and is implemented as part of the larger multi-country ToGETHER program. The second phase aims at further promoting and enhancing local partners' leadership in the program and in the humanitarian system of Pakistan in provinces of Sindh, Punjab, Balochistan and KP, focuses capacity strengthening and sharing on anticipatory humanitarian action, emergency preparedness, coordination and people-centred approaches, increases the flexible funding component known as HOIFA, and fosters advocacy for a so-called 'locally led localization'.
